facts.quote: The native place of Narayan Meghaji Lokhande was Kanhesar near Saswad in Pune district.

facts.quote: He formed the mill workers union known as 'Bombay Mill Hands Association' in 1890. This workers union is believed to be the beginning of organised movement in India.

facts.text: Lokhande was the chairman of the Mumbai branch of the Satyashodhak Samaj founded by Mahatma Phule.
facts.quote: He was also the chairman of Mumbai branch of Satyashodhak Samaj founded by Mahatma Phule.

facts.quote: Due to his efforts, from 10 June 1890, the workers started getting weekly holiday on Sunday.

facts.quote: The Socialist youths, while they were in prison at Nasik, decided to form the Socialist Party within the Indian National Congress.

facts.text: In the Quit India movement of 1942, the young socialists were in the forefront.
facts.quote: In Quit India movement of 1942, these young socialists were in the forefront.

facts.quote: Shripad Amrut Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Keshav Neelkanth Joglekar etc. were arrested. They were charged with planning of a conspiracy to overthrow the British rule. ... The trial took place at Meerut and is therefore known as the 'Meerut Conspiracy Case'.

facts.text: Women were given a secondary position; male reformers took initiative in reform for women, and in time women leaders came forward.

facts.text: Pandita Ramabai established the 'Arya Mahila Samaj' and 'Sharda Sadan'; 'Seva Sadan' was founded by Ramabai Ranade.

facts.quote: Rakhmabai Janardan Save was the first practicing woman doctor in India. She delivered series of lectures related to health issues of women. She also opened a branch of Red Cross Society at Rajkot.

facts.text: After the Act of 1935, women were included in the Provincial Ministries; the Constitution of India clearly states equality of men and women.

facts.text: Dr. Anandibai Joshi was the First Indian Female Doctor; the death of her son, who lived only ten days, inspired her to study medicine.

facts.quote: She acquired M.D. degree in 1886.

facts.quote: While returning to India Anandibai contracted tuberculosis. Later on 16 February 1887 she died in Pune.

facts.text: Following Mahatma Phule's teachings, Gopal Baba Walangkar and Shivram Janba Kamble worked to eradicate untouchability; Mahatma Jyotirao Phule and Narayan Guru awakened people against injustice to Dalits.

facts.text: The three restrictions of the caste system: Rotibandi (no inter dining with certain castes), Betibandi (no intercaste marriages) and Vyavasaybandi (no pursuing certain occupation).
facts.quote: Prohibition of inter dining with certain castes (Rotibandi), prohibition of intercaste marriages (Betibandi), prohibition of pursuing certain occupation (Vyavasaybandi).

facts.text: Shahu Maharaj ate food from the hands of Dalit people and passed the Act of inter caste marriage in his State.

facts.text: On 22 February 1918 Shahu Maharaj abolished the 'Balutedari System' by a declaration in the Government Gazette of Kolhapur, giving freedom of occupation.

facts.text: The Justice Party did valuable work for social equality in South India.
facts.quote: The Justice Party did valuable work for social equality in South India.

By taking inspiration from him Amrutlal Vitthaldas Thakkar alias Thakkar Bappa, Appasaheb Patwardhan etc. these activists dedicatedly worked for equality.

facts.text: Babasaheb Bole got a bill passed in the Bombay Provincial Assembly to open public water reservoirs to the untouchables; Dr. Ambedkar started the Satyagraha at Chavdar lake in Mahad and burned the Manusmriti.

facts.text: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar started newspapers like 'Muknayak', 'Bahishkrut Bharat', 'Janata' and 'Samata'.
